41695-the-appendages-anatomy-and-relatio.creator: Charles Schuchert.
41695-the-appendages-anatomy-and-relatio.description: A book by Charles Schuchert.. e fossils and have long attracted the attention of amateur collectors and men of science. These "three-lobed minerals" have been mentioned or described in books at least since 1698 and now several thousand species are known to palæontologists. To this group of students they are the most characteristic animals of the seas of Palæozoic time, and even though they are usually preserved as dismembered parts, thousands upon thousands of "whole ones" are stored in the museums of the world.

arxiv-2007-13641.title: Evaporation-induced crystallization of surfactants in sessile multicomponent droplets
arxiv-2007-13641.creator: Yaxing Li, Valentin Salvator, Herman Wijshoff, Michel Versluis, Detlef Lohse
arxiv-2007-13641.description: Abstract Surfactants have been widely studied and used in controlling droplet evaporation. In this work, we observe and study the crystallization of sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) within an evaporating glycerol-water mixture droplet. The crystallization is induced by the preferential evaporation of water, which decreases the solubility of SDS in the mixture.

arxiv-2205-07965.title: Flexible and curtailable resource activation in three-phase unbalanced distribution networks
arxiv-2205-07965.creator: Md Umar Hashmi, Arpan Koirala, Hakan Ergun, Dirk Van Hertem
arxiv-2205-07965.description: Abstract The need for flexibility and curtailable resources is crucial for ensuring the healthy operation of future distribution networks (DN). In this work, we propose a network-state driven framework that distribution system operators (DSOs) can utilize for activating flexible and curtailable resources for alleviating network voltage and thermal issues, while accounting for network voltage and current imbalances.

arxiv-2205-14648.title: Non-Uniform Convergence in Moment Expansions of Integral Work Relations
arxiv-2205-14648.creator: Hila Katznelson, Saar Rahav
arxiv-2205-14648.description: Abstract Exponential averages that appear in integral fluctuation theorems can be recast as a sum over moments of thermodynamic observables. We use two examples to show that such moment series can exhibit non-uniform convergence in certain singular limits. The first example is a simple model of a process with measurement and feedback.

arxiv-2212-08861.title: DAG: Depth-Aware Guidance with Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
arxiv-2212-08861.creator: Gyeongnyeon Kim, Wooseok Jang, Gyuseong Lee, Susung Hong, Junyoung Seo, Seungryong Kim
arxiv-2212-08861.description: Abstract Generative models have recently undergone significant advancement due to the diffusion models. The success of these models can be often attributed to their use of guidance techniques, such as classifier or classifier-free guidance, which provide effective mechanisms to trade-off between fidelity and diversity.

arxiv-2406-03199.title: Bayesian WeakS-to-Strong from Text Classification to Generation
arxiv-2406-03199.creator: Ziyun Cui, Ziyang Zhang, Guangzhi Sun, Wen Wu, Chao Zhang
arxiv-2406-03199.description: Abstract Advances in large language models raise the question of how alignment techniques will adapt as models become increasingly complex and humans will only be able to supervise them weakly. Weak-to-Strong mimics such a scenario where weak model supervision attempts to harness the full capabilities of a much stronger model.

arxiv-2408-13343.title: FSUDAQ - A general purpose GUI data acquisition program for the CAEN x725, x730, x740 digitizers
arxiv-2408-13343.creator: T. L. Tang
arxiv-2408-13343.description: Abstract FSUDAQ is a versatile, multi-threaded, lightweight data acquisition software with a graphical user interface, designed to fully utilize the capabilities of first-generation CAEN x725, x730, and x740 series digitizers equipped with various Digital Pulse Processing (DPP) firmware, including Pulse-Height Analysis (PHA), Pulse-Shape Discrimination (PSD), and Charge-Digital Conversion (QDC). It emphasizes user-friendliness, stability, scalability, high throughput, and low latency.

arxiv-2505-21100.title: The Correlation Thresholding Algorithm for Exploratory Factor Analysis
arxiv-2505-21100.creator: D. S. Kim, A. Lu, and Qing Zhou
arxiv-2505-21100.description: Abstract Exploratory factor analysis is often used in the social sciences to estimate potential measurement models. To do this, several important issues need to be addressed: (1) determining the number of factors, (2) learning constraints in the factor loadings, and (3) selecting a solution amongst rotationally equivalent choices. Traditionally, these issues are treated separately.

arxiv-2506-02005.title: Pruning for Performance: Efficient Idiom and Metaphor Classification in Low-Resource Konkani Using mBERT
arxiv-2506-02005.creator: Timothy Do, Pranav Saran, Harshita Poojary, Pranav Prabhu
arxiv-2506-02005.description: Abstract In this paper, we address the persistent challenges that figurative language expressions pose for natural language processing (NLP) systems, particularly in low-resource languages such as Konkani. We present a hybrid model that integrates a pre-trained Multilingual BERT (mBERT) with a bidirectional LSTM and a linear classifier.

arxiv-2602-07706.title: Dense Feature Learning via Linear Structure Preservation in Medical Data
arxiv-2602-07706.creator: Yuanyun Zhang, Mingxuan Zhang, Siyuan Li, Zihan Wang, Haoran Chen, Wenbo Zhou, Shi Li
arxiv-2602-07706.description: Abstract Deep learning models for medical data are typically trained using task-specific objectives that encourage representations to collapse onto a small number of discriminative directions. While effective for individual prediction problems, this paradigm underutilizes the rich structure of clinical data and limits the transferability, stability, and interpretability of learned features.

pmc-10532561.description: The technological, social and economic development observed in recent decades brought an exponential increase in consumption and inherent new challenges. Recycling is one of the best solutions to minimize the environmental impact of raw materials. However, multi-material components are difficult or even impossible to recycle.

pmc-11479324.title: Deep Recyclable Trash Sorting Using Integrated Parallel Attention
pmc-11479324.creator: Hualing Lin, Xue Zhang, Junchen Yu, Ji Xiang, Hui-Liang Shen, Anastasios Doulamis
pmc-11479324.description: Sorting recyclable trash is critical to reducing energy consumption and mitigating environmental pollution. Currently, trash sorting heavily relies on manpower. Computer vision technology enables automated trash sorting. However, existing trash image classification datasets contain a large number of images without backgrounds. Moreover, the models are vulnerable to background interference when categorizing images with complex backgrounds.

pmc-11646654.title: Ventricular septal defect characteristics influence presence of septal anatomical isthmuses in patients with repaired tetralogy of Fallot
pmc-11646654.creator: Justin Wallet, Yoshitaka Kimura, Nico A Blom, Mark G Hazekamp, Margot M Bartelings, Monique R M Jongbloed, Katja Zeppenfeld

pmc-11654190.title: Respiratory physiotherapy for critically ill children: concern regarding a recommendation
pmc-11654190.creator: Nobuaki Shime
pmc-11654190.description: The guideline entitled “Japanese Clinical Practice Guidelines for Rehabilitation in Critically Ill Patients 2023” was published by the Japanese Society of Intensive Care Medicine in 2023. However, there is an issue with the clinical question and recommendation for respiratory physiotherapy in mechanically ventilated children.

pmc-12457860.title: Exploring Online Health Information–Seeking Behavior Among Young Adults: Scoping Review
pmc-12457860.creator: Kristine Stifjell, Torkjel M Sandanger, Charlotte Wien, Javad Sarvestan, Yam B Limbu, Nathaniel Godwin
pmc-12457860.description: BackgroundThe ability to access and evaluate online health information is essential for young adults to manage their physical and mental well-being. With the growing integration of the internet, mobile technology, and social media, young adults (aged 18-30 years) are increasingly turning to digital platforms for health-related content.

pmc-12877134.title: Intrinsic asymmetric iontronic-interfaces for giant power generation
pmc-12877134.creator: Haiyan Wang, Jie Dang, Ying Wang, Feng Liu, Jinguo Lin, Tiancheng He, Qihua Liao, Qi Zhang, Huhu Cheng, Liangti Qu
pmc-12877134.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Iontronic power source harnesses ion-electron coupling effect for energy conversion, offering great potential in wearable electronics and bioelectronics. However, its limited power density and insufficient current hinder the progress toward commercialization. Here we report an iontronic electricity generator based on intrinsic asymmetric interfaces and controllable energy-release, which reaches a maximum volumetric power density of up to 3680 W m-3, area power density of 18.4 W m-2, and peak current of more than 5 A.

pmc-13050147.title: Navigating rare terrain: successful management of subscapular and deltoid hematomas via the dorsal scapular approach
pmc-13050147.creator: Saad Riaz, Osama Ijaz, Yasir Hidayat, Abdur Rehman, Abdul Wahab, Ali Asad Ullah, Rahmat Gul Omarzai
pmc-13050147.description: Subscapular hematomas are rare entities that pose diagnostic and therapeutic challenges due to their deep anatomical location and nonspecific presentation. Delayed recognition may lead to abscess formation and long-term functional impairment. We report the case of an 18-year-old male who presented with progressive pain, swelling, and restricted range of motion of the right shoulder following blunt trauma.

pmc-13175813.title: Bioinformatics-driven insights: rapamycin-mediated CaMK2D inhibition alleviates intestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury
pmc-13175813.creator: Ruxiang Sheng, Yanqiu Liang, Huihong Zhang, Yonghe Lai, Haiyun Hong, Dingbang Huang, Dezhao Liu
pmc-13175813.description: IntroductionIntestinal ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury, a common and severe clinical condition with high morbidity and mortality, burdens healthcare systems. Our previous investigations established that a nano-delivery system enabled targeted rapamycin delivery to intestinal I/R injury sites with therapeutic efficacy. While calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase IIδ (CaMK2D) has been implicated in myocardial injury and tumorigenesis, its role in intestinal I/R pathophysiology remains unexplored.

pmc-13231063.title: Venous-trapezium coupler anastomosis in a partially congested combined ALT/TFL-flap: A case report
pmc-13231063.creator: S Gorji, P Stammer, A Dermietzel, T Hirsch, P Wiebringhaus
pmc-13231063.description: BackgroundReconstruction of large soft tissue defects with extensive vascular trauma remains a challenge. Intraosseous cannulation, commonly used in emergency medicine, may offer a novel solution for venous outflow. We report the use of the trapezium bone for venous drainage in a combined anterolateral thigh and tensor fasciae latae (ALT/TFL) flap reconstruction.

pmc-13241569.title: Breed-specific divergence in boar sperm regulatory profiles involves piRNA and mitochondrial small RNAs
pmc-13241569.creator: Anna Asratian, Signe Isacson, Unn Kugelberg, Colum P Walsh, Anita Öst
pmc-13241569.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Small non-coding RNAs (sRNAs) act as post-transcriptional regulators and protectors of genomic integrity. Environmental stress and genomic variation can both alter the sRNA composition in sperm, leading to altered offspring phenotypes. Commercial pig breeds, which have undergone years of selective breeding, vary in purpose: some are optimized for meat production, others for high reproductive capacity – traits that are often antagonistic.

pmc-13332766.title: Abnormal Brain Structure and Function in People with Shoulder Pain: A Systematic Review of Neuroimaging Studies
pmc-13332766.creator: Bin Fan, Ching Shan Lam, Shuqi Chen, Chun Liang Hsu, Arnold Yu Lok Wong, Karen McCreesh, Tak Man Wong, Hio Teng Leong
pmc-13332766.description: BackgroundShoulder pain (SP) is a prevalent musculoskeletal disorder. Emerging evidence suggests maladaptive brain plasticity in individuals with SP. This systematic review summarized structural and functional brain abnormalities in individuals with SP and explored their associations with clinical outcomes.MethodsPubMed, Web of Science, EBSCO, and EMBASE were searched from inception to June 2025.

pmc-13393248.title: A qualitative exploration of clinicians’ experiences and perceptions of a well-being leadership development training program
pmc-13393248.creator: Kristi L. Roybal, Tricia T. James, Laura L. Chun, Karina M. Squire
pmc-13393248.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundHealthcare worker burnout is a national challenge, with implications for healthcare worker well-being and mental health, the quality of patient care, and healthcare costs. The Clinician Wellness Council (CWC), a 15-month well-being leadership development training program, was designed and implemented to provide practicing clinicians (“CWC members”) across several clinical groups within the Providence health system with skills, coaching, and community to address the local drivers of their clinical groups’ burnout.
